name: Anki
what: Free open-source flashcard program with spaced repetition scheduling, now using FSRS as an optional scheduler.
learner: Self-directed adults, heavy in medical students and language learners
mechanism: User-made or shared flashcards reviewed at intervals set by SM-2 or FSRS
business_model: Free desktop and Android apps, paid iOS app funds development; stewardship moving to AnkiHub since Feb 2026

price.text: Desktop free; AnkiMobile iOS $24.99 one-time in the US store (checked 2026-09-08 by a third party)

offline_desktop: native desktop app (Windows, Mac, Linux), works offline, local data, optional AnkiWeb sync

efficacy.design: Cross-sectional survey plus institutional score records, n=165 respondents of 887 (Step 1 scores for 99), University of Minnesota, 2023
efficacy.sponsor: University of Minnesota Medical School grant and student council
efficacy.finding: Daily Anki users had median USMLE Step 1 of 238 vs 233.5 for non-daily users (P=.039); no difference on Step 2 (250 vs 251, P=.440). Authors say the link may reflect more total study time.

ai_features_2026: No built-in AI in core Anki; AI comes through add-ons and AnkiHub
does_not_do: No source canon, no knowledge graph, no research workflow; card content quality depends on the user or shared decks
note: No official user count exists; Anki forum threads say the developers do not publish download counts. AnkiDroid alone reported about 400,000 unique users in 2024 (forum roundup, search snippet). FSRS benchmark (fetched from GitHub, run by the FSRS authors, so treat as developer-run): 9,999 collections and 349,923,850 reviews; log loss FSRS-6 0.3460, FSRS-5 0.3561, FSRS-4.5 0.3625, HLR 0.4694; RMSE bins FSRS-6 0.0653 vs HLR 0.1275. The benchmark measures recall prediction accuracy, it does not measure learning outcomes. A 2026 systematic review (Springer, snippet) says high-frequency Anki users beat minimal users by 4 to 13 Step 1 points and calls the evidence largely observational. A Rocky Vista cohort found 223.71 vs 222.58 with no significant correlation (snippet, PMC8651966 or PMC10403443).

(2) Kestin, Miller, Klales, Milbourne, Ponti, Scientific Reports 15:17458, 2025 (PMC page fetched): randomized crossover in Harvard Physical Sciences 2, fall 2023, 233 enrolled and 194 eligible; custom GPT-4 tutor 'PS2 Pal' with pre-written step-by-step solutions versus in-class active learning. Median post-test 4.5 (AI) vs 3.5 (in-class), pre-test median 2.75; effect 0.63 SD by linear regression, 0.73 to 1.3 SD by quantile regression; median AI time 49 minutes against an assumed 60 in class. Authors declare no competing interests; the page states no funder. It tested a purpose-built tutor in one course over two weeks. (3) Kosmyna et al., MIT Media Lab, arXiv:2506.08872 (v1 2025-06-10, v2 2025-12-31), preprint with no journal reference on the arXiv page: 54 participants in three essay sessions split into LLM, search-engine and brain-only groups, 18 completed a fourth crossover session; EEG connectivity was weakest in the LLM group, and LLM users reported the lowest essay ownership and struggled to quote their own essays.
